content.text:
## The API changed, and the values are gone for good

On 2026-10-28, Artificial Analysis switched to **Intelligence Index v5**. I traced it day by day through the `history/` snapshots on the `data` branch:

| Snapshot | Index version | Models with intelligence | coding | agentic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10-27 | 4.3 | 704 | 258 | 167 |
| 10-28 | 5 | 77 | 258 | 167 |
| 10-29 → 11-16 | 5 | 78 → 129 | **0** | **0** |

Their docs say plainly: *"Artificial Analysis no longer publishes a Coding Index or an Agentic Index."* The fields are still in the response, always null and marked deprecated.

**What the API offers now (free tier):**
- **`artificial_analysis_intelligence_index`:** only about 129 of 742 models have been re-scored on v5. Older models such as gpt-5.x, glm-5/5.1 and kimi-k2.x have none.
- **Six new Capability Indexes:** finance, strategy & ops, legal, healthcare, **engineering** and economics, each with about 100–143 models. The docs don't say what goes into the Engineering Index, so it may not mean software engineering.
- **`artificial_analysis_intelligence_index_cost.cost_per_task.total_cost`:** what one Index task costs to run, for 121 models. It reflects how many tokens a model actually uses. Only the total is on the free tier, not the input/reasoning/answer split.
- **`performance_v3`:** mean tokens per second, for 399 models. The median we use today covers 386.

**What this does to scoring now:** in [compute-scores.ts](src/scoring/compute-scores.ts), a missing metric counts as 0. So `codingIndex` and `agenticIndex` add nothing for any model, and that's 70% of the weight in `agenticCoding` and 50% in `softwareFactory`. Models with no v5 intelligence score still get ranked on speed and cost alone. As a result, every category ends up favouring fast, cheap models: Haiku 5.5, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, MiMo Flash, all scoring around 0.13–0.17.

---

❓ **Q1** - **Replace coding/agentic with what?** Options:
- (a) Drop both and use `intelligenceIndex` as the main quality signal.
- (b) Use `engineeringIndex` as a stand-in for coding, without knowing what it measures.
- (c) Combine (a) and (b): intelligence plus engineering.
- (d) Pull in another benchmark source for coding or agentic work, such as SWE-bench or Terminal-Bench leaderboards.

➡️ (c), and drop `codingIndex`/`agenticIndex` from the code and config completely. Engineering is the closest free signal and it covers about the same models as intelligence. Before we lean on it, I'll check that it tracks the old coding index on models that have both scores.

---

❓ **Q2** - **Models without a v5 intelligence score:** today they're kept and ranked on speed and cost alone. Should we require `intelligenceIndex` and skip a model when it's missing?

➡️ Yes, require it. A model with no quality score shouldn't be recommended. This drops older models like gpt-5.4 until AA re-scores them, which is the honest outcome.

---

❓ **Q3** - **Cost model:** options:
- Keep today's per-token blended price with `outputToInputRatio`.
- Switch to a "cost per task" figure: multiply the provider's blended price by a verbosity factor, `cost_per_task / AA's own blended price`. This catches models that are cheap per token but burn through tokens.

➡️ Yes, switch to cost per task. It fixes the main blind spot in cost efficiency, and it only uses fields available on the free tier.

---

❓ **Q4** - **Speed source:** keep `performance.median_output_tokens_per_second`, and fall back to `performance_v3.mean_output_tokens_per_second` when the median is missing?

➡️ Yes. Most models have the median, and the fallback fills a few gaps.

---

❓ **Q5** - **Catch this kind of breakage next time:** the pipeline ran green for 19 days while scoring nothing. If any weighted metric is null for every candidate, should the run fail (or at least show a warning on the site)?

➡️ Yes, fail the run. The workflow already keeps the last good site when a run fails, and that beats publishing quiet nonsense. We should also fail when `intelligence_index_version` changes, so a person checks the new version.

---

Once these are settled, the next round covers the new weights for each category, how the site shows the replaced columns, and whether old snapshots or the `notes` text need updating.

Before writing round 2, I ran the check I promised in round 1. For each model scored in both snapshots, I compared the old v4.3 indexes (2026-10-27) with today's v5 indexes:

| Old (v4.3) | New (v5) | Models | Pearson | Spearman |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| coding | intelligence | 48 | 0.85 | 0.96 |
| coding | engineering | 48 | 0.84 | 0.95 |
| agentic | intelligence | 48 | 0.86 | 0.90 |
| agentic | strategy & ops | 61 | 0.96 | 0.94 |
| **v5 intelligence** | **v5 engineering** | 129 | **0.995** | **0.995** |

Within v5, Engineering is almost a copy of Intelligence. All the v5 indexes rank models in nearly the same order, and they rank them about the same way the old coding and agentic indexes did. So on the free tier there's really one quality score, and the scoring comes down to quality vs. cost vs. speed.

---

❓ **Q1** - **Change round 1's answer: Intelligence only, no Engineering?** Adding Engineering would just count the same signal twice and use up one of the 129 slots for models that have both scores.

➡️ Yes. Use `intelligenceIndex` as the only quality metric.

---

❓ **Q2** - **New weights per category (quality / cost / speed):**

| Category | Quality | Cost | Speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| agenticCoding | 0.70 | 0.15 | 0.15 |
| codeReview | 0.85 | 0.10 | 0.05 |
| softwareFactory | 0.45 | 0.30 | 0.25 |
| llmWiki | 0.60 | 0.30 | 0.10 |

➡️ Yes, use these. Each category gets its own trade-off, and they roughly follow what each category weighted before the coding and agentic indexes went away.

---

❓ **Q3** - **Keep four categories?** With only one quality metric, agenticCoding and codeReview now differ only in their weights, so their shortlists may come out the same. The other option is to merge them.

➡️ Yes, keep all four. The categories describe what the user is trying to do, and the weights still separate them. If the lists end up the same, that's useful to know too.

---

❓ **Q4** - **Keep `outputToInputRatio` next to the verbosity factor?** The plan for cost is: provider blended price at the category's ratio × verbosity factor, where verbosity = AA `cost_per_task` ÷ AA's own blended price. The ratio sets the input/output mix for each category. The factor measures how many tokens a model uses compared with other models.

➡️ Yes, keep both. llmWiki's 0.2 ratio is still the right input/output mix for that category.

---

❓ **Q5** - **Models with an intelligence score but no `cost_per_task`** (about 8 models): should they get the median verbosity factor across candidates and be flagged as estimated, rather than skipped?

➡️ Yes, use the median and flag it as estimated. Skipping them would drop models that already have good quality data.

❓ **Q6** - **Site table columns:** in [index.html](site/index.html), should we drop the Agentic/Coding columns, show **Intelligence / Cost per task / Speed**, and add the AA index version next to the fetch date?

content.text:
Got it. Models with no `cost_per_task` will be dropped. That leaves three small questions, and once they're answered every decision is settled.

❓ **Q1** - **Models with no speed figure:** some models have an intelligence score and a cost per task but no speed in either the median or the v3 data (for example `qwen4-max`). Should we drop them too? That would match your Q5 answer: no estimated or zero-filled data.

➡️ Yes, drop them. The partial-scoring path and `missingMetrics` go away completely, so every candidate that gets scored has all three inputs.

---

❓ **Q2** - **Models whose AA pricing is missing or zero:** without AA's own blended price we can't work out the verbosity factor. Should we drop these too, under the same rule?

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q3** - **How to ship it:** should this go on a branch with a PR, not straight to `main`?

➡️ Yes, use a branch and a PR. The changes span scoring, config and the site, so they're worth reviewing before the daily run picks them up.

---

### Full design, for you to confirm

- **Quality:** `intelligenceIndex` only. Remove `codingIndex` and `agenticIndex` from the types, the config and the site. Don't use Engineering, because it correlates with Intelligence at r=0.995.
- **Cost:** provider blended price at the category's `outputToInputRatio` × verbosity factor. The factor is AA `cost_per_task.total_cost` ÷ AA's blended price at the same ratio. Cost efficiency is still 1 ÷ that cost, normalized min–max.
- **Speed:** `performance.median_output_tokens_per_second`, falling back to `performance_v3.mean_output_tokens_per_second` when the median is missing.
- **Which models get scored:** a model needs all of intelligence, `cost_per_task`, AA pricing and speed. Otherwise it's skipped with a warning.
- **Weights (quality / cost / speed):** agenticCoding 0.70/0.15/0.15 · codeReview 0.85/0.10/0.05 · softwareFactory 0.45/0.30/0.25 · llmWiki 0.60/0.30/0.10. Keep all four categories.
- **Guards:**
  - `expectedIntelligenceIndexVersion: 5` goes in `categories.json`. If AA reports a different version, the run fails.
  - The run also fails if any metric with weight is null for every candidate.
- **Site:** show Intelligence / Cost per task / Speed columns, plus the AA index version next to the fetch date.
- **Docs:** rewrite the `notes` in `categories.json`. Leave `history/` untouched.
- **Ship:** a branch and a PR, after the typecheck → lint → format → `npm start` loop passes.

Typecheck, lint and format are clean, and I ran the scoring step on today's `data` branch snapshot. I haven't run the full `npm start` (no `AA_API_KEY` here) or opened the updated site in a browser.

**Why values were missing:** Artificial Analysis switched to Intelligence Index v5 on 2026-10-28. Since 2026-10-29 its API returns the Coding and Agentic indexes as null for every model, and their docs say they won't come back. Our scoring counted them as 0, so the pipeline kept passing for 19 days while those weights scored nothing.

**What changed:**
- **Scoring** ([compute-scores.ts](src/scoring/compute-scores.ts)): models are now ranked on intelligence, cost per task and speed. A model missing any of those, or missing AA's pricing, is skipped instead of scored as 0. That leaves 61 models scored, down from 121.
- **Guards:** the run now fails if AA reports an Intelligence Index version other than 5, if a category weights a metric that doesn't exist (a leftover `codingIndex` weight, for example), or if no model can be scored. I tested the first two by hand and both fail with a clear message.
- **Config** ([categories.json](config/categories.json)): the new weights, the pinned version, and rewritten notes explaining why coding and agentic are gone.
- **Site** ([index.html](site/index.html)): the Agentic and Coding columns are replaced by Intelligence, $ per task, tokens per second and $ per 1M tokens, and the header shows the index version.

**Top picks today for agentic coding:**

| Provider | Picks |
|---|---|
| Copilot / OpenCode Zen | Gemini 4 Carbon, Claude Opus 5.5 |
| OpenCode Go | Gemini 4 Argon, Kimi K3.1 Pro |
| ClinePass | Kimi K3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 |

**Two things to know before merging:**
- **Agentic coding and code review now give the same shortlists**, as expected now that they differ only in their weights.
- **`outputToInputRatio` now does almost nothing.** Cost per task is AA's measured cost × (provider price ÷ AA price) at the same ratio. When a provider charges AA's list price, which is true for most models today, the ratio cancels out. So the LLM Wiki category's 0.2 ratio no longer makes its costs reflect its read-heavy use. Fixing that properly needs AA's input/output token split, which is only on the paid tier.
